1.why: The UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with adequate letter and line spacing across all screens.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case without italics or all-caps, though some info boxes contain multi-sentence blocks.

3.why: Layouts are single-column, responsive, and remain legible and well-spaced at mobile width.

4.why: Most instructions are short plain-language sentences, with only the demo info boxes slightly longer.

5.why: No explicit examples of expected input format are shown beside fields (e.g., code patterns); only placeholders like a phone number appear.

6.why: Users can proceed via short labels and buttons without reading long passages; info boxes are optional context.

7.why: The setup secret and backup codes are displayed as selectable text so they can be copied, but no dedicated copy button is provided.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative is offered; authenticator setup is manual-entry only.

9.why: Standard form inputs allow browser autofill for email/phone, but no explicit password-manager or one-time-code autocomplete attributes are evidenced.

10.why: Page titles, primary blue CTAs, and step headings clearly highlight the current step and main action.

11.why: Each screen focuses on one primary task, though the final settings page presents several secondary actions together.

12.why: Green confirmation banners and log messages plainly state what happened and the next step after each action.

13.why: Users can re-request challenges, generate replacement codes, navigate back, and retry verification without penalty.

14.why: No error-message examples appear in the screenshots, so it is not shown that errors explain the problem and fix without blame.

15.why: No countdown timers or reading time limits are visible on any step; code entry appears untimed.
